card.name: Closing punctuation after citations and credentials
card.fires_on: Closing parentheses or commas right after section-number citations like (5.1) or after credentials like Ph.D., plus scattered other words at clause boundaries. The common thread is a point where a reference or aside ends and the main sentence resumes.

modes.label: Closing citation parenthesis
modes.description: A closing bracket after reference or section numbers in label highlights or study citations.
modes.example: 5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS • Severe neutropenia : See Boxed Warnings ( 5.1<< )>> • Gastrointestinal Hypomotility

modes.label: After credentials or foreign gloss
modes.description: A comma or parenthesis closing a credential or a transliterated gloss, just before the sentence continues.
modes.example: According to Richard L. Huganir, Ph.D<<.,>> a Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigator and chair

modes.label: Scattered sentence words
modes.description: Ordinary words such as this, has, reporting or death in news or label prose.
modes.example: In a heartbreaking case of parental neglect, a 12-year-old girl in Scotland<< has>> been admitted to a hospital after a life

card.plain: It fires where a citation or aside closes and the sentence picks back up, with no single clear meaning.
